$schema_note: Machine-readable companion to STYLE_GUIDE.md. Hand this file and TEMPLATE.html to an AI model together with a description of the physics you want. The human guide has the reasoning; this has the rules.

file_rules.external_requests: none: no scripts, fonts, stylesheets, images, analytics, or CDN links
file_rules.file_name: kebab-case slug matching the sims.js entry, e.g. sims/rolling-race.html

color_roles.--body: the primary object under study (a ball, the test body, the boat)
color_roles.--twin: a comparison object drawn in grey
color_roles.--ghost: predicted, theoretical, or osculating paths; drawn dashed
color_roles.--conj / --ball: a secondary moving object or event markers
color_roles.--star: the single warm accent; the Sun, a launch point, focus rings on the index page

fonts.--serif: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, "Book Antiqua", Georgia, serif
fonts.--sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

usage.sans: controls, labels, readout values, all canvas text

layout.hover_effects: none beyond colour change on buttons

components.button_primary: background var(--ink); color #fff; border 1px solid var(--ink); radius 4px; padding 6px 14px
components.segmented: div.seg containing buttons with aria-pressed; selected = ink background, white text
components.tabs: div.tabs[role=tablist] > button[role=tab][aria-selected]; underline in --ink for the selected tab
components.range: 22px round ink thumb, 4px --rule track, 28px hit height; label on the left, value with units on the right in span.val
components.readout: div.readout > div cards: .k label (muted), .v value (18px), .f formula (serif, muted)
components.notes: div.notes with What to try. paragraph, then assumptions and units

page_structure_in_order: h1 (short noun phrase; no 'simulation' in the name)
p.lede (2-4 sentences: what you see, what will happen, the key physics claim)
div.tabs (only if there are genuinely different screens)
div.transport: Play/Pause button, Reset button, time scrubber (analytic sims), playback speed control (when needed)
div.readout: numbers with formulas, in HTML not on the canvas
div.controls: sliders with labels and live values
div.toggles: checkboxes for views and overlays
div.notes: 'What to try', then assumptions and units
physics_rules: Model functions first in the script, clearly named, equations in comments beside them.
Prefer closed-form solutions where they exist; they make scrubbing exact.
Use symplectic integration (leapfrog / kick-drift-kick) for orbits and oscillators; fixed small step; remove bodies that leave the domain instead of propagating NaN.
Any time acceleration, exaggerated parameter, or schematic representation must be stated on screen; exaggerations are sliders that start at the real value.
Show a limiting-case check in the readout when possible (predicted vs simulated).
Pause the loop when document.hidden; cap integration steps per frame so slow devices degrade gracefully.
interaction_rules: Slider changes apply immediately; analytic sims reset t to 0 on parameter change.
One Play/Pause button whose label changes; Reset returns to t = 0 with current parameters.
Playback speed labelled in physical terms ('planet orbits per second', '0.4x slow motion').
Default the view that makes the main point; default overlays on.
canvas_rules: Draw in CSS pixels: ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0); compute layout from the canvas's actual CSS size each frame.
Fit the scene from a bounding box of the whole run so nothing goes off-canvas.
Predicted paths dashed; trails solid and fading with age.
Every moving thing keeps one colour across scene, plot, legend, readout.
Below 560px wide: drop label text on vectors, shorten captions, label every other tick; keep arrows.
Canvas text 12-13px in screen pixels at all sizes.
accessibility_rules: Respect prefers-reduced-motion: start paused or animate only on user action.
Real HTML controls with labels; aria-pressed on segmented buttons; role=tab/aria-selected on tabs.
Never distinguish two things by colour alone; vary line style or shape too.
writing_rules: Plain words, short sentences, present tense, written for a student.
Name things by what they are ('the planet'), not by code names ('the perturber').
Buttons say what happens; status text reports state.
No exclamation marks, no emoji, no hype.

manifest_entry_schema.title: string
manifest_entry_schema.topic: one of: kinematics, dynamics, rotation, oscillations, thermo, em, optics, modern, astronomy, materials
manifest_entry_schema.blurb: 1-2 sentences, what it shows and the main thing to notice

submission_checklist: Opens from a local file with no network and no console errors
Physics functions at the top; textbook limiting case reproduced
Assumptions, units, time acceleration, exaggerations stated on the page
Usable at 390px wide with readable labels
Reduced motion respected; loop pauses when hidden
Home link, GPL header, 'What to try', readouts with formulas present
sims.js entry added with a real date
Tried by someone other than the author for two minutes without instructions
prompt_for_ai_generation: See PROMPT.md in the repository for the full prompt and a worked example. Short form: attach style.json and TEMPLATE.html; describe the physics in one paragraph (what is on screen, what happens, what is adjustable, what the student should notice, what if anything is exaggerated); require the model at the top of the script with equations in comments, units and assumptions on the page, HTML readouts with formulas, a 'What to try' paragraph, offline operation, 390px usability, and the GPL header with provenance; ask for the limiting cases checked and the sims.js entry.
